chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, and Safwan, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:
I asked him about a slave man marrying four free women. He said: No, but he can marry two free women, and if he wishes, he can marry four slave girls.
ai.seo_question: What is the maximum number of wives a male slave can marry according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the marital capacity of a male slave (abd), distinguishing between the restriction of marrying four free women versus the permission to marry four slave women. It reflects the juristic principle that a slave's limited property and status restrict his ability to maintain multiple free wives, while allowing greater flexibility with slave wives who share his dependent status. This ruling is often discussed in the context of how social hierarchy influences the application of the 'four wives' limit in Shia fiqh.
